verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Parwanoo engineering units with captive power backup and diversified order books; avoid power-sensitive continuous-process units and any borrower exposed to the Bajaj Electricals exit.
title: Parwanoo Engineering & Capital Goods: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Parwanoo's engineering units convert steel, plastics and power into castings, fabricated structures, wire and components, sold to OEMs and EPC contractors. **Cash sits in receivables and inventory, not in the machine** — the ICRA methodology note is explicit that a longer working-capital cycle means a larger funding requirement [9]. National demand is real: IIP NIC 28 output is +10.3% YoY and +10.4% Apr-to-date [D]. So when a proposal lands, check the receivable days and inventory turns first; if the cycle is stretching, ask what changed in the customer mix.

## What has broken locally
**Parwanoo's local signals are weak while the national sector is strong.** Himachal GST collections are -22.8% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand is -6.8% against India +9.5% [D]. The Tribune reports the state sold 600 MW to Kerala, with unscheduled load shedding, low voltage and an effective power shortage of 20% [3]. Bajaj Electricals has permanently closed its Parwanoo unit [2] — note that filing is dated 2022, so treat it as history, not fresh news. **For a continuous-process unit, power tripping is a direct cash loss**; investors are installing transformers, stabilisers and UPS, which raises cost of production [3].

## Where to grow
**Pursue component and fabrication suppliers to national demand, not local-demand-dependent units.** Peer results show the order book is where the money is: DEE's order book crossed Rs 1,300 crore with Q3 revenue up 77% to ₹286.7 crore [5]; Skipper posted its highest-ever Q2 revenue with PAT up 56% [6]; Pitti is commissioning a Hyderabad facility backed by order visibility from data centres, mining, off-highway and railways [4]. So when a proposal lands, check the order book and customer concentration; if one buyer is above half of sales, ask for the contract tenure. Avoid units whose only edge was cheap Himachal power [3].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the power risk and the receivable cycle.** Take monthly: power-backup evidence (DG set, stabiliser, UPS), GST returns, and a receivables ageing. Where the unit runs continuous process, ask for a load-shedding log; if outages exceed what the borrower budgeted, resize the drawing power. Rating literature flags that EPC cash conversion cycles run higher than OEMs [11], so price term loans to the longer cycle. Collect from customer: actual power cost per unit and the share of production lost to tripping.

## Early-warning signs
- **GST turnover falling faster than the state's -22.8% [D] (monthly)** -> freeze enhancement, ask for the buyer-wise sales register.
- **Receivable days rising two months running (monthly)** -> shift part of the limit to LC-backed or bill-discounted structure.
- **Load-shedding hours rising or DG diesel spend spiking (monthly)** -> recheck unit economics before renewal.
- **Order book thinning or one client crossing half of sales (quarterly)** -> reduce tenor, seek personal guarantee.

days rise two months running -> move to LC/bill-discount structure
outage hours exceed budget -> resize drawing power
